Analyse the platform dynamics.
1.  A ball can be in positions 1, 2 or 3.  Only the ball struck by the matching-number piston is “ejected” (a win); any ball occupying position 1 when piston 2 or 3 fires is merely released (no win).
2.  Let E₁, E₂, E₃ be the probabilities a ball is eventually ejected, starting from positions 1, 2, 3.
   • From position 1: E₁ = ⅓  (piston 1) → ejected, ⅔ → released ⇒ E₁ = ⅓.
   • From position 2: ⅓ (piston 2) ejects immediately; ⅔ moves to position 1 ⇒ E₂ = ⅓ + ⅔·E₁ = ⅓ + ⅔·⅓ = 5⁄9 ≈ 0.556.
   • From position 3: ⅓ (piston 3) ejects immediately; ⅓ moves to pos 2; ⅓ moves to pos 1 ⇒ E₃ = ⅓ + ⅓·E₂ + ⅓·E₁ = ⅓ + ⅓·5⁄9 + ⅓·⅓ = 17⁄27 ≈ 0.630.
   Thus a ball starting in position 3 has the highest chance of being ejected.
3.  At the very start of the game the only ball guaranteed to begin in position 3 is Ball 3 (balls 1 and 2 start in positions 1 and 2).  All later balls enter in positions 2 or 3 with probabilities 0.4 and 0.6, giving them an average ejection chance of 0.6 – lower than Ball 3’s 0.630.
Hence Ball 3 maximises the probability of being ejected and therefore of winning the prize.
